uncertain

uncertain is a package for performing uncertainty of measurement calculations. These calculations are used in the validation of genetic laboratory tests to communicate the variability within an assay.

However, the specific calculations required are sometimes unclear, and there is a lack of worked examples relating to genomic testing. uncertain aims to address this by providing functions for key calculations, and example datasets which reflect the data structures encountered in genomic laboratories.

Calculating uncertainty

uncertain is based on the instructions for pooled standard deviation analysis described in the publication “Selected Laboratory and Measurement Practices and Procedures to Support Basic Mass Calibrations” from the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NISTIR 6969). The functions are tested using example calculations from the NIST Engineering Statistics Handbook.

uncertain includes example datasets for copy number variant and single nucleotide variant repeatability data.

library(uncertain)
library(ggplot2)

The key function is group_stats which calculates statistical variation within the dataset based on grouping variables (i.e. sample, gene) provided by the user.


cnv_variation <- group_stats(data_cnv,
            measurement_variable = dosage,
            sample, gene)

knitr::kable(cnv_variation[[1]])
sample gene mean standard_deviation conf_int_95_min conf_int_95_max replicates degrees_freedom sum_squares standard_error

Sample 1 CDKN2A 2.0279581 0.0449833 1.9807510 2.0751651 6 5 0.0101175 0.0183643
Sample 1 EGFR 1.9847034 0.0689010 1.9123962 2.0570105 6 5 0.0237367 0.0281287

Sample 2 CDKN2A 0.4979573 0.0444423 0.4513179 0.5445966 6 5 0.0098756 0.0181435
Sample 2 EGFR 2.0284635 0.0695623 1.9554623 2.1014647 6 5 0.0241946 0.0283987

group_stats also calculates the pooled standard deviation for the whole dataset.


cnv_variation[[2]]
#> [1] 0.06910729

Installation

You can install the development version of uncertain from GitHub with:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("joe-m-shaw/uncertain")
